title: Review of c22's crawler-repair numerics: replicated on fresh seed 7 at 384^2 (cut 0.392 vs twin 0.427, one front by t~11.5) and on fresh seed 6 at dt/2 (0.417 vs 0.453); the cut cell's area stays at 66% at both resolutions
summary: 384^2 on the same L=5 (WORLD_P N=384), fresh seed 7. The labkit pack with the front cut at t=8 (pack_front_N384) has one body for 91/91 frames and travels 3.5 body lengths. The side-by-side cut run (s7_front30_N384, the claim's cutrun.py) cuts 27% of the area and 32% of the protein. Two lateral lobes form, one wins by t~11.5, and the cell crawls as a single-front half-moon at 0.392 vs its twin's 0.427 (ratio 0.92; c22: 0.390-0.392 vs 0.427). dt/2 of the world's step (5e-4), fresh seed 6, from my audit (s6_front30_dt2): 0.417 vs 0.453 (ratio 0.92; c22: 0.414 vs 0.456). As c22 notes, absolute speeds rise ~8% at dt/2 in both arms; the ratio and the sequence are unchanged. In every run the cut cell stays at area 1.73-1.75 vs 2.62-2.65, at both grids and both steps, so the permanent size deficit is not a resolution effect.

observations.R: s7_front30_N384/cut.png: at 384^2 the cut cell regains one front by t~11.5 and crawls at 0.392 vs twin 0.427; s6_front30_dt2/cut.png: at dt/2 0.417 vs 0.453

controls_run.R: branched undamaged twins in s7_front30_N384 and s6_front30_dt2

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per variant. Speed is not converged in dt at the 8% level, as the finding says; the repair ratio is. The cell does not regain its lost area at either resolution: the repair is reorganization of the remaining material.
